steps.title: Create an Account on Axis Hub
steps.body: Go to the Axis Hub and sign up with email, Google, X, or a wallet.

steps.title: Complete Pre-Training Tasks
steps.body: Pick a task from the Hub, such as picking, placing, or stacking objects in a kitchen or home scene, and steer the simulated arm through it. Your demonstration is judged on success, efficiency, and motion smoothness. Failed attempts are never uploaded and carry no penalty, so retry until the run feels clean.

steps.title: Take On Post-Training Tasks
steps.body: Here a trained policy attempts the task while you watch, and you grab control only when it fails. Sessions have a 30-second takeover budget: incomplete attempts score zero, while runs the policy finishes untouched score highest. Short, precise corrections at the failure point score best.

steps.title: Sign Your Submissions On-Chain
steps.body: Open your Portfolio and sign each completed task on Base. Signing is what makes a submission count toward Axis Points.

steps.title: Spread Your Tasks Across Scenarios and Skills
steps.body: Diversity is measured on two axes, the scenes your tasks cover and the skills they exercise, so vary both rather than repeating one combo. The Hub also caps each task at 5 completions per account, and anything past the cap is excluded from scoring.

steps.title: Join Alliance Tasks for Partner Rewards
steps.body: Check the Alliance section for tasks built with ecosystem partners such as BitRobot. These pay Axis Points plus a partner reward under campaign terms, the best value per session when one is live.

steps.title: Invite Contributors Who Will Stay Active
steps.body: Share your referral link from the Hub. Only direct invitees count, and only through what they produce, so ten inactive signups earn you nothing while one steady contributor keeps paying.

steps.title: Complete Challenger Tasks in Axis Hub
steps.body: Open your Portfolio page in Axis Hub and check the “Seek the Unseen” badge. A lit badge means you are on the current whitelist. Open the Challenger Program zone and review the week’s task list. Complete and sign a task as usual. The zone is visible to everyone, but only whitelisted users can open the task interface.

The official docs say Points will be one input in a planned Community Contributor Airdrop, with eligibility, allocation, and timing to be published before any claim event.
